prep.understand: Laravel reads .env.production at runtime in production mode. Stripe has TWO separate key sets (test sk_test_* vs live sk_live_*) — the live keys are what go here. Chatwoot needs the API URL + an operator token. Mail needs real SMTP credentials. Never commit this file to git.

Grab Stripe LIVE mode keys from Stripe dashboard → Developers → API keys (publishable + secret)
Copy the Chatwoot API URL and operator access token from Chatwoot → Settings → Access Token
SSH into azteam-vps and write /opt/azteamai-system/.env (chmod 600); run `php artisan config:cache` and verify with `php artisan about`

Chatwoot instance → Settings → Access Token

tasks.notes: Reconciliation gate BLOCKS go-live (spec §7 step 4). Extract ReconciliationGateService + billing:reconcile-cutover artisan command; idempotent/rerun-safe; prints per-client breakdown; 'PASS' is the only proceed signal.

prep.what: Build a `billing:reconcile-cutover` artisan command that verifies the imported billing data matches azteam_crm ground truth — PASS required before go-live.
prep.understand: The import (t38) already ran and loaded projects/versions/invoices into the new system. Reconciliation checks two axes: (1) each client's open AR balance (Σ balance_due) equals azteam_crm's open balance, and (2) next-charge dates for recurring projects match. This command must be rerun-safe — running it twice gives the same result. A single per-client breakdown row + a final PASS/FAIL verdict.
approach: Find CrmImporter::reconcile() (~L277) — this is the logic to extract into ReconciliationGateService
Create `app/Console/Commands/ReconcileCutoverCommand.php` (make:command billing:reconcile-cutover); inject ReconciliationGateService
Command loop: for each client, query both DBs (new system + azteam_crm) and compare open AR and next-charge date; print per-client row; print PASS or FAIL+diff at end
Run it, fix any discrepancies (wrong totals usually mean the import missed a record or rounded differently), rerun until PASS
resources: app/Services/CrmImporter.php ~L277 (reconcile logic to extract)
azteam_crm DB connection (config/database.php — check for a secondary connection)
`php artisan make:command ReconcileCutoverCommand` scaffold

tasks.notes: DONE: Agency + AgencyMembership + Tenant.agencyId + User.isSuperAdmin + agency-of-one seed + provisionAgencyOfOne. REMAINING: agency authz policy, AgencyRole runtime validation, denormalized agencyId + cross-agency invariant on agent-owned models, agency-isolation tests.

prep.what: Close out t6 by building the agency authorization policy layer, AgencyRole validation, denormalized agencyId on agent-facing models, and agency-isolation tests.
prep.understand: The data model is done (Agency, AgencyMembership, Tenant.agencyId). What's missing is the POLICY layer: the app needs to enforce that calls are authorized for the caller's agency, and that every agent-facing model also carries agencyId alongside tenantId (defense-in-depth for cross-agency isolation + rollups). The tests must prove two agencies can't see each other's data — same isolation pattern as the existing test:tenants suite.

Write a Prisma migration adding `agencyId` to each agent-facing model (those in TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS that agents write to); add a DB CHECK or application-layer assertion that child.agencyId == parent.agencyId
Add agency-isolation tests: provision agency A + agency B, create data under each, query as A's token — assert B's data is not returned

tasks.title: pending_outbound approval state machine + DB guard
tasks.notes: DONE: PendingOutbound model + DB CHECKs + queueForApproval + assertDispatchable guard (7 checks green). REMAINING: approve/decline/expire transitions, authenticated one-time token consumption, claim->deliver->mark-sent worker.

prep.what: Complete the pending_outbound flow: approve/decline/expire state transitions + the authenticated one-time token consumption + the claim-then-deliver-then-mark-sent Inngest worker.
prep.understand: The guard/model foundation is solid. The remaining piece is the FLOW: (1) a secure approve/decline endpoint that consumes a one-time token (crypto.randomBytes, hashed in DB, single-use); (2) an expire path that marks messages as expired after deadline; (3) an Inngest job that claims an approved PendingOutbound (atomic UPDATE WHERE status='approved'), delivers via ChannelRouter, marks sent. The 'human-approval = sole external-send trigger' invariant must hold — assertDispatchable gates the delivery.
approach: Add `approvalToken` (random hex, hashed in DB) + `expiresAt` to PendingOutbound; generate on queueForApproval
Build POST /api/outbound/approve?token=... and /api/outbound/decline?token=... routes — verify token hash, check not expired/consumed, transition status, mark consumedAt

Add an Inngest function `deliver-approved-outbound`: SELECT WHERE status='approved' AND approvedAt IS NOT NULL → atomic UPDATE SET status='delivering' → call assertDispatchable → ChannelRouter.send() → UPDATE SET status='sent'
Add an Inngest cron to expire overdue pending items: UPDATE SET status='expired' WHERE expiresAt < now() AND status IN ('queued', 'approved')
Extend test:outbound to cover the approve/decline/expire paths and the claim idempotency (concurrent delivers should not double-send)
resources: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') for token generation, SHA-256 for storage
Inngest docs: functions + cron triggers (app/api/inngest/route.ts)
ChannelRouter seam (lib/channels/router.ts) for the actual send call

tasks.title: Observability: Sentry + Inngest dashboard lockdown + payload scrub
tasks.notes: SERVICES §9 / P&S §3.5. Sentry error monitoring with token+PII scrubbing; lock the Inngest dashboard (allow-list) + scrub secrets from job payloads. Healthchecks.io heartbeat lands with t19.

prep.what: Wire Sentry error tracking with PII scrubbing, lock down the Inngest dashboard to prevent secret/payload leakage, and add a Healthchecks.io heartbeat.
prep.understand: Standard Sentry setup is fine for error capture, but the non-obvious parts are: (1) the `beforeSend` hook must scrub any field that could carry a secret (token, secret, dek, key, password) before events hit Sentry's servers; (2) the Inngest dashboard shows full job payloads by default — if job payloads carry tenant data or tokens, locking it down prevents a 'Horizon-dashboard' footgun where anyone with the URL can read job internals.
approach: Run `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs` to scaffold Sentry in the Next.js app; add SENTRY_DSN to .env
In sentry.server.config.ts add a `beforeSend` hook: strip any event property whose key matches /token|secret|dek|key|password/i from both `extra` and `request.data`
In the Inngest serve handler (app/api/inngest/route.ts) add `signingKey: process.env.INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` — this gates the dashboard to signed requests only; document the env var in .env.example
Register a Healthchecks.io heartbeat ping at the end of your longest cron job (e.g., the cleanup or expire cron) so you get alerted when it stops running
resources: @sentry/nextjs package (npm install @sentry/nextjs)
Sentry docs: Next.js SDK + beforeSend callback
Inngest docs: `signingKey` option on the serve() handler
Healthchecks.io (free tier) — create a check, get the ping URL, add a fetch call to your cron
